findings.issue_text: EventManager.ts:117-118 — missing optional chaining on `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` after destructuring `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` causes a TypeError crash when destinationCalendar is null/empty, making booking creation 500 instead of falling back to Cal Video for events with Google Meet location

googlecalendar CalendarService.ts:255-257 (updateEvent) and :314-317 (deleteEvent) — fallback branch is dead code: the `find` only executes when externalCalendarId is falsy so it can never match, always producing `calendarId: undefined` and 'Missing required parameters: calendarId' errors, silently leaving Google events stale or orphaned after reschedule/cancel

organizations/create.handler.ts:151 — condition inverted in unrelated drive-by change: `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}` reverses the original `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` logic, breaking org creation entirely when billing is disabled (missing required slug) and bypassing the slug-approval/verification flow when enabled

Non-Google calendar services (office365calendar CalendarService.ts:72-76, larkcalendar CalendarService.ts:127-129, BaseCalendarService CalendarService.ts:156-160) always target `destinationCalendar[0]` instead of the destination/credential being processed, so collective bookings create duplicate events on host A's calendar, never create events on host B's calendar, and mixed integrations build invalid API paths that fail silently

Null-credentialId destination calendars never match GoogleCalendarService.ts:148-151's `find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)`, so event creation falls back to "primary" instead of the configured externalId and CalendarManager.ts:267 stores references without externalCalendarId, making those events impossible to update or delete

EventManager.ts:~478, 530 — `credential` declared outside the reference loop leaks across iterations in `update()`: it retains the previous iteration's value when a credentialId can't be resolved, and one unresolvable credential causes getCalendar(undefined) to throw and abort every host's update

handleCancelBooking.ts:~424-431 — DB-fetched credential passed to `getCalendar` without `include: { app: ... }` (unlike EventManager which constructs appName), so canceling a booking whose calendar credential belongs to another host silently no-ops and the event is never removed from that host's calendar

handleCancelBooking.ts:~437-455 — recurring-cancel block sits inside the reference loop so it runs N times with N references (duplicate delete calls, second pass 404s), while the inner `references.find` still only handles each remaining booking's first reference, leaving orphaned events on secondary hosts' calendars

handleNewBooking.ts:~1063-1073 — members' destination calendars silently dropped when the organizer has none: the ternary yields `null` making the subsequent `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...)` a no-op, inconsistent with other call sites that fall back to `[]`

EventManager.ts:~558 — merge path deletes only the first old calendar reference via `references.find((reference) => reference.type.includes("_calendar"))`, orphaning events on all other hosts' calendars after a merge/reschedule replaces a collective booking

handleNewBooking.ts:~990-1000, 1071 — no dedup of destination calendars: shared team calendars produce duplicate entries, causing createAllCalendarEvents to call createEvent twice with the same credentialId and create two identical events on that calendar

handleNewBooking.ts:~750-763 — `loadUsers` catch masks root causes: non-HttpError/non-Prisma errors become generic unlogged 500s, Prisma errors are rethrown as 400s with raw driver messages, and the new early-throw on empty `dynamicUserList` changes behavior so empty dynamic lists now surface as 500s

Missing ownership check when loading credentials from DB by ID in EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents, the EventManager update path, and handleCancelBooking — the new fallback fetches any credential by ID (including its OAuth key) without validating it belongs to a booking participant, enabling potential credential abuse/IDOR and cross-account calendar writes using another user's OAuth tokens

Inverted slug gating in organizations/create.handler.ts — changing `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug }` to `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}` inverts the condition so unverified organizations claim their slug immediately, bypassing the verification-gated slug-assignment flow (and orgs get no slug at all when billing is disabled)

Null-deref crash in EventManager Google Meet fallback (EventManager.ts:117-118) — `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` throws a TypeError when destinationCalendar is null or empty; the old code used optional chaining, so booking creation can 500 instead of falling back to Cal Video

Google CalendarService updateEvent/deleteEvent dead-code find — the predicate `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` compares against a falsy externalCalendarId so it can never match, making selectedCalendar/calendarId always undefined and causing update/delete to fail for bookings without a stored externalCalendarId

Non-Google providers (Lark, Office365, CalDAV) ignore per-host destination calendars — they still use destinationCalendar[0] regardless of which host's credential is in use, so collective bookings create events on the wrong host's calendar; per-host targeting is only implemented for Google

handleCancelBooking DB credential fallback is a silent no-op — the raw credential is fetched without including the app relation or mapping appName, so getCalendar (which dispatches on credential.appName) returns null and deleteEvent never runs, leaving orphaned calendar events on hosts' calendars

Merge/reschedule path deletes only the first calendar reference — the single `find` for a `_calendar` reference doesn't handle collective bookings that now carry multiple per-host calendar references, so remaining hosts' old events are orphaned

Team destination calendars silently dropped when organizer has none — evt.destinationCalendar is set to null instead of [] so the push of teamDestinationCalendars no-ops, and the booking row only connects destinationCalendar[0].id so members' destination calendars are not persisted for later cancel/reschedule flows

Serialized external calendar API calls per host in the booking-creation hot path (packages/core/EventManager.ts:337-366, createAllCalendarEvents): the `for (const destination of event.destinationCalendar)` loop awaits `createEvent` sequentially instead of collecting promises and using `Promise.all`, causing booking-request latency to grow ~N × one calendar API call for collective events with N hosts, while the adjacent no-credentialId branch still parallelizes

Multiplicative, duplicated delete calls when canceling recurring collective bookings (packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:424-470): the recurring-event cancellation branch iterating all user calendar credentials × all remaining recurring bookings sits inside the new per-reference loop, executing R×C×B external delete calls instead of C×B, with (R−1)×C×B exact duplicates that will 404/410 after the first succeeds, and re-running `getCalendar` (service construction + credential-key decryption) R×C times; the branch should be hoisted out of the reference loop since it doesn't use the outer reference's own uid/externalCalendarId

N+1 `prisma.credential.findUnique` queries inside the new loops (three instances: packages/core/EventManager.ts:341-357 per destination, packages/core/EventManager.ts:508-528 per calendar reference in the update path, packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:430-440 per calendar reference): each loop issues one `findUnique` with an `app` join per element whose credential isn't already in memory; should be batched with a single `findMany({ where: { id: { in: [...] } } })` before each loop, especially since two instances are in the booking create/cancel hot paths

Dead fallback in Google `updateEvent`/`deleteEvent` (packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:253-256 and :312-315): the expression `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` can never match in the fallback branch because `externalCalendarId` is falsy there, so the `find` predicate compares `externalId === <falsy>` and always yields `undefined`; since EventManager passes `calenderExternalId` as null when a booking reference has no stored externalCalendarId, those updates/deletes now go out with `calendarId: undefined` and fail, where the old code fell back to `destinationCalendar.externalId`

Inverted condition in org creation (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts:148-151): `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` became `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, flipping behavior in both branches — with team billing disabled, organizations no longer get a `slug` at all, and with it enabled, `slug` is now set alongside `requestedSlug`, bypassing the previous pending-approval flow

Inverted flag condition in packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts:151 — the rewrite of `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` inverts the condition: with team billing disabled (typical self-hosted), orgs are created with no slug, causing the public org-creation endpoint to 500 since Team.slug is required; with billing enabled, slug is set immediately, bypassing the requestedSlug verification/approval flow (unverified orgs can occupy slugs).

Breaking webhook payload shape change with no versioning — booking webhook payloads (BOOKING_REJECTED, and by construction BOOKING_CREATED/UPDATED/reschedule/cancel events) now emit destinationCalendar as an array instead of null | object, so external subscribers accessing payload.destinationCalendar.integration or .externalId silently get undefined; a documented public integration surface changed with no versioning, migration note, or compat period.

Dead fallback in Google CalendarService updateEvent/deleteEvent (packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:253-256 and 312-315) — in the fallback branch externalCalendarId is falsy, so `find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` compares a non-null string to a falsy value and can never match, always evaluating to undefined; bookings whose calendar reference lacks externalCalendarId (legacy bookings, or new bookings created via the no-credentialId path in EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents) will send calendarId: undefined to the Google API on reschedule/cancel, causing update/delete failures and orphaned calendar events.

Non-Google calendar services (packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:72-75, packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:127-128, packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:156-162) ignore the new credentialId parameter and always target destinationCalendar[0] (the organizer's calendar) — for multi-host collective events, the member's credential is used to write to the organizer's calendar, causing Graph/Lark/CalDAV auth or 404 failures, while the booking reference records the member's externalId so later updates/deletes target a calendar where no event exists; the per-host destination feature is broken for every provider except Google.

Reschedule merge path in packages/core/EventManager.ts (~583-585) still uses `find` to locate only the first _calendar reference while this PR makes creation produce multiple _calendar references (one per host destination) — when update() is called with newBookingId (booking merge on reschedule), only one old calendar event is deleted and the other hosts' calendars keep stale/orphaned events.

Google createEvent silently falls back to "primary" and can duplicate events (packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:145-155) — when a destination has no credentialId (nullable on DestinationCalendar), createAllCalendarEvents calls createEvent once per matching-type credential, and Google's find(cal => cal.credentialId === credentialId) fails for each, so every credential creates on "primary" (duplicate events on the wrong calendar); additionally createEvent(c, event) is called without externalId so the stored reference has externalCalendarId: undefined.

Missing optional chaining crashes EventManager.create on empty/null destinationCalendar (packages/core/EventManager.ts:116-118) — `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` is accessed without `?.`, and this PR makes []/null a normal value for destinationCalendar, so a Meet-location booking/confirmation with an empty destination calendar throws TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined, causing a 500.

handleCancelBooking DB-fetched credential lacks appName for getCalendar (packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:~432-441) — the fallback passes the raw Prisma Credential to getCalendar, unlike the parallel new code in EventManager.ts which deliberately reconstructs { appName: app.slug, ... }; this path is now reachable for collective bookings whose references carry member credentialIds, so canceling a multi-host booking can fail to resolve the calendar service and leave member-host events undeleted.

Breaking change to exported contract types without compat (packages/types/Calendar.d.ts:171, 221) — CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar changed from DestinationCalendar | null to DestinationCalendar[] | null, and Calendar.createEvent gained a required credentialId: number parameter; every consumer of these exported types (app-store packages, external code importing @calcom/types) that reads destinationCalendar.externalId or calls createEvent(event) breaks at compile time, with no deprecation, overload, or version bump for the package signature.

requestReschedule drops the user.destinationCalendar fallback its sibling handlers have (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/requestReschedule.handler.ts:239-242) — the old copy-paste bug `bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar || bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar` was preserved instead of restoring the intended `|| user.destinationCalendar` fallback that handleCancelBooking, confirm, and editLocation all implement, so reschedule-request evts get [] while every other handler gets the user's calendar.

handleNewBooking uses null (not []) and silently discards members' destination calendars (packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1063-1067, 1072-1073) — when both eventType.destinationCalendar and organizerUser.destinationCalendar are null, evt.destinationCalendar is null so evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars) no-ops and collected team members' destination calendars are silently dropped (the exact scenario this PR is meant to fix), inconsistent with the [] fallback used in every other handler.

loadUsers error handling leaks Prisma messages and swallows errors (packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:~755-762) — PrismaClientKnownRequestError is re-thrown as 400 with the raw error.message (internal DB details exposed to the public booking API), and all other errors become a generic 500 "Unable to load users" with no logging of the cause, changing the error-response contract and losing diagnosability.

Google CalendarService updateEvent/deleteEvent fallback is dead code: the find fallback only runs when externalCalendarId is falsy and then searches for a calendar whose externalId equals undefined/null, which can never match, so calendar.events.update/delete is called with calendarId undefined and guaranteed fails; this path is reachable via legacy bookings and new bookings created in the no-credentialId branch of createAllCalendarEvents (packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts ~256 and ~315)

CalendarManager.createEvent accepts the new externalId param but never forwards it to the calendar service; Lark, Office365, and the CalDAV base service all read destinationCalendar[0], so for multi-host bookings the 2nd+ hosts' events are attempted on the first host's calendar ID with the wrong host's token (403/404) and never appear on their own calendars (packages/core/CalendarManager.ts ~227-257)

EventManager.update calls updateEvent(credential, ...) with a possibly-undefined credential, lacking the if (credential) guard that createAllCalendarEvents has, so getCalendar(undefined) throws, Promise.all rejects, and one host's deleted/missing credential converts every reference's result to failure, breaking calendar sync for all hosts on reschedule (packages/core/EventManager.ts ~540)

Calendar update failures are now completely silent: the catch block in EventManager.update removed console.error(message) with no replacement (no log.error or error report), so multi-host reschedules can no-op with zero observability (packages/core/EventManager.ts ~596)

The catch in EventManager.update returns calendarReference?.map(...) ?? [], so a throw before calendarReference is assigned returns [], indistinguishable from 'nothing to update', whereas previously it always returned a success: false result (packages/core/EventManager.ts ~596)

Reschedule-merge still deletes only the first old calendar reference: booking.references.find() on type including '_calendar' was left as find while bookings now carry multiple calendar references (one per host), so the newBookingId merge path deletes only one host's old event and orphans the remaining hosts' stale events on their calendars (packages/core/EventManager.ts ~573)

Google createEvent 'primary' fallback changes behavior for destinations without credentialId: old code used destinationCalendar.externalId when present, new code matches by credentialId and falls back to 'primary', so events go to each matching credential's primary instead of the configured calendar, and with two same-type credentials both now succeed on their own primary, producing duplicate events (packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts ~150)

Unrelated logic inversion in org creation: (...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })) became (...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})), so self-hosted installs (IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED=false) no longer get a slug at all (broken org URLs) while billing-enabled orgs get both slug and requestedSlug, bypassing the requested-slug flow (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts:151)

handleCancelBooking's DB-credential fallback fetches prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id } }) without include: { app } and assigns it raw, unlike the parallel EventManager fallback which includes app and maps appName, so getCalendar may resolve to null and calendar?.deleteEvent silently no-ops, leaving stale events on the host's calendar (packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts ~425-435)

Recurring collective cancellation ignores per-reference credentials: the recurring branch sweeps bookingToDelete.user.credentials (organizer only) regardless of which reference is being processed, so team hosts' calendar events are never deleted when a recurring collective booking is canceled (packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts ~437-460)

The recurring cancellation sweep now executes once per calendar reference, so with N references each remaining event is deleted N times, with the second pass guaranteed to error (caught and logged) (packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts ~437-460)

Non-calendar (video) booking references no longer persist credentialId: 'credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined' replaced the previous 'result.credentialId' fallback, so video references lose the credential that created them (packages/core/EventManager.ts ~169)

Unsafe dereference in packages/core/EventManager.ts:117-119: when destinationCalendar is null, undefined, or an empty array (all valid per the new type), the destructured mainHostDestinationCalendar is undefined and accessing .integration throws a TypeError that aborts booking creation; the line needs mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration.

Dead/self-contradictory fallback in packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:255-258 and 315-317: in the else branch externalCalendarId is falsy, so find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId) can never match and the fallback always evaluates to undefined, sending calendarId: undefined to the Google API on update/delete for references lacking externalCalendarId (legacy bookings and new bookings from the no-credentialId branch) — a behavioral regression versus the old fallback to event.destinationCalendar.externalId.

The ternary booking.destinationCalendar ? [booking.destinationCalendar] : user.destinationCalendar ? [user.destinationCalendar] : [] is copy-pasted ~10 times across read sites (bookingReminder.ts, webhook.ts, paypal-webhook.ts, handleCancelBooking.ts, confirm.handler.ts, editLocation.handler.ts, deleteCredential.handler.ts, requestReschedule.handler.ts); the root cause is the DB schema (Booking/User/EventType.destinationCalendar) still being scalar while the domain type is now an array (handleNewBooking.ts:1873-1877 persists only destinationCalendar[0]) — extract a shared helper and/or migrate the schema before the duplication drifts.

The ~20-line block that fetches a credential via prisma.credential.findUnique and manually remaps it field-by-field to CredentialWithAppName is duplicated verbatim in EventManager.ts:343-364 (createAllCalendarEvents) and :503-527 (update), with a third variant in handleCancelBooking.ts:425-434 that omits the app include — extract a single getCredentialById() helper.
Separation-of-concerns smell in EventManager: it was previously a pure orchestrator over injected calendarCredentials but now queries Prisma directly mid-loop, blurring its boundary.

In packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:437-457, the recurring-cancellation branch is completely independent of reference yet sits inside the for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference) loop, so an N-reference booking runs the whole recurring deletion N times (duplicate deleteEvent calls per updated booking, second call 404s) — the branch belongs outside the loop.
In the recurring-cancellation branch of handleCancelBooking.ts, the outer const calendar = await getCalendar(calendarCredential) is dead (shadowed by the inner const calendar), a wasted call.

updBooking.references.find(...) in handleCancelBooking.ts still takes only the first calendar reference of each updated booking, so collective members' events on other references are not cleaned up on cancellation.

Multi-host destination-calendar selection is implemented only in GoogleCalendarService; Lark (larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:128-130, 163-165, 192-194, 237-239), Office365 (office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:73-76), and BaseCalendarService (packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:156-163) destructure destinationCalendar[0] and use its externalId while EventManager invokes them once per host with that host's credential, so for a collective event with two non-Google hosts, host B's credential is used against host A's calendarId (wrong calendar or API error) — the collective-multi-host feature only works end-to-end on Google.

The reschedule-merge path in packages/core/EventManager.ts (~551-555) still uses booking.references.find((reference) => reference.type.includes('_calendar')), which returns only the first calendar reference; since this PR creates one _calendar reference per host, only the first host's old event is deleted on reschedule-merge and the remaining hosts' old events are orphaned on their calendars as stale events.

In packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1080-1082, evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars) is a no-op when evt.destinationCalendar is null (lines 1063-1067), silently discarding team members' destination calendars in exactly the collective case the PR targets; it should be evt.destinationCalendar = [...(evt.destinationCalendar ?? []), ...teamDestinationCalendars].

In handleNewBooking.ts, teamDestinationCalendars is populated via side effects inside map callbacks, making correctness depend on the later await Promise.all having already run — fragile temporal coupling.

The new externalId? parameter on CalendarManager.createEvent (packages/core/CalendarManager.ts:219-221, 267-270) is a pure pass-through that never influences event creation and is only echoed into the return object, so it can record a calendar the event was not actually created on (Google falls back to 'primary' when the credentialId find misses).
credentialId: result.credentialId ?? undefined at EventManager.ts:169 and 208 is dead code because result.credentialId is always set.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/requestReschedule.handler.ts:237-240 still misses the user.destinationCalendar fallback: the original line was a copy-paste bug (bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar || bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar), and the rewrite kept only the first operand instead of fixing the fallback to user?.destinationCalendar as in every sibling handler, so reschedule requests for bookings without a booking-level destination calendar lose the calendar context.

Three different empty representations for destinationCalendar now coexist — null (handleNewBooking.ts:1063-1067), [] everywhere else, and the type at packages/types/Calendar.d.ts:171 allowing undefined | null | [] — forcing consumers to defend against all three with inconsistent checks (?? [] vs && length > 0); pick one canonical empty value (ideally [] or non-nullable) and enforce it.

The Google-specific credentialId parameter leaked into the generic Calendar interface's createEvent (packages/types/Calendar.d.ts:221): Lark/Office365/BaseCalendarService do not declare it and silently ignore it, and updateEvent solves the same selection problem with a different mechanism (externalCalendarId), leaving two divergent selection strategies in one interface contract.

The loadUsers rewrite in handleNewBooking.ts:724-762 swallows errors: the catch block converts every unexpected error into a generic 500 'Unable to load users' (masking root causes) while leaking raw Prisma error messages to the client as 400, and the dynamicUserList guard error also becomes a 500 instead of the presumably-intended 400.

Unrelated changes are mixed into the PR — the loadUsers rewrite (handleNewBooking.ts:724-762), organizations/create.handler.ts:148-152 ternary rewrites semantically identical to the spread-of-false they replace, a CalendarManager.ts:230 spelling change, and a handleNewBooking.ts:370 typo rename — and belong in separate commits/PRs.

Inverted condition in `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts:151`: `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` was rewritten to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, a logical inversion — when the flag is false, organizations are created with no slug at all (a required column, so Prisma throws and org creation 500s entirely), and when the flag is true, `slug` is written directly, bypassing the `requestedSlug` approval/verification gating

Dead-code fallback in Google `CalendarService.ts` updateEvent (253-256) and deleteEvent (314-317): the fallback branch only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy but then searches for a calendar whose `externalId === externalCalendarId` (a guaranteed null/undefined), so the find can never succeed and the API call is made with `calendarId: undefined` — booking references without a stored `externalCalendarId` (which this PR itself manufactures via the no-credentialId path in `createAllCalendarEvents`) can no longer be updated or deleted from Google, leaving stale/orphaned events after reschedule/cancel; the predicate should be `cal.credentialId === credentialId`

Only Google resolves the destination calendar per credential: Lark (`larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:127,161,190,237`), Office365 (`office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:71-75`), and CalDAV (`lib/CalendarService.ts:156-162`) services were only mechanically converted to use the first destination's `externalId` regardless of which host's credential is creating the event, so for collective events secondary hosts' event creation fails (swallowed into `success: false`) or lands on the wrong calendar, and references are persisted pointing at calendars where no event exists

Google `createEvent`/`updateEvent` hardcode the organizer email to the first destination's `externalId` even when writing host B's calendar, misattributing the organizer on every non-first host's copy

Silent skip in `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` (`packages/core/EventManager.ts:~341-365`): when a destination's `credentialId` is set but the credential is neither in `this.calendarCredentials` nor found in the DB, the `if (credential)` block simply doesn't run — no else, no log, no failure result — so a host whose credential was deleted/disconnected gets no calendar event and no trace while the booking completes 'successfully'

`evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` in `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:~1075-1077` no-ops when the base array is null (when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists), silently discarding every team member's destination calendar; the array should be initialized, e.g. `evt.destinationCalendar = [...(evt.destinationCalendar ?? []), ...teamDestinationCalendars]`

Confirmation and payment-success flows (`confirm.handler.ts:175-179`, `payments/api/webhook.ts:118-120, 228-230`, `paypal-webhook.ts:152-156`) rebuild the `CalendarEvent` from `booking.destinationCalendar` (the single Prisma relation, which `handleNewBooking` only populates with `evt.destinationCalendar[0]`) and never reconstruct the multi-host array, so collective bookings requiring confirmation or payment create calendar events only on the organizer's calendar and the other hosts get nothing

`EventManager.update` catch block (`packages/core/EventManager.ts:~595-607`): if the throw happens before `calendarReference` is assigned (e.g., the `newBooking` Prisma query fails), the catch returns `calendarReference?.map(...) ?? []` — an empty array instead of the previous guaranteed `success: false` result row — so a thrown update can be recorded as a no-op

`EventManager.update` catch block: when a failure happens mid-loop (e.g., `updateEvent` rejecting for one member's unresolvable credential via `Promise.all`), the catch marks every reference `success: false`, turning a partial failure into a total failure — one bad host poisons updates for all other hosts' calendars

Partial deletion of multi-reference bookings: the merge-delete on `newBookingId` (`EventManager.ts:~555-557`) and the recurring-cancel branch (`handleCancelBooking.ts:~437-450`) still use `.find(...)` first-match-only on the now multi-element reference set, and recurring-cancel iterates only the organizer's credentials (members' credentials are never consulted) — after reschedule/cancel of a collective booking, the other hosts' calendars keep stale events

Credentials fetched from DB by raw ID with no ownership validation (`EventManager.ts:~341-357` and `~505-530`, `handleCancelBooking.ts:~425-441`): `prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id } })` uses whatever row comes back without checking that the credential belongs to the booking's user/hosts, expanding the trust boundary from fail-closed to fail-open — a malicious user could point their destination calendar at any credential ID in the database and have bookings write to or cancel/update another user's calendar using their OAuth tokens; needs explicit `userId`/`teamId` scoping on the DB fetch

`requestReschedule.handler.ts:240-242` preserves the `bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar || bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar` copy-paste bug in the rewritten line — the missing `user.destinationCalendar` fallback remains in place, making this handler inconsistent with all sibling handlers in the PR that got the fallback

`organization: { select: { slug: true } }` dropped from the non-eventType user query in `loadUsers` (`handleNewBooking.ts:~727-735`), so `user.organization` becomes undefined for dynamic-link bookings unless `userSelect.select` already includes organization, silently breaking downstream consumers of the organizer's org slug

goldens.comment: A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.
The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.

Logic inversion in organization creation: The slug property is now conditionally set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, instead of when it's false as originally intended. This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled

The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).

The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.

When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (the else branch), the predicate compares `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` (undefined/null), so it will not find a normal calendar externalId and yields `undefined`. Unlike createEvent (which explicitly falls back to `"primary"`), these update/delete paths now lose the prior fallback to `event.destinationCalendar.externalId` and can pass an undefined calendarId to the Google API, causing broken updates/deletes for references lacking externalCalendarId.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The ternary booking.destinationCalendar ? [booking.destinationCalendar] : user.destinationCalendar ? [user.destinationCalendar] : [] is copy-pasted ~10 times across read sites (bookingReminder.ts, webhook.ts, paypal-webhook.ts, handleCancelBooking.ts, confirm.handler.ts, editLocation.handler.ts, deleteCredential.handler.ts, requestReschedule.handler.ts); the root cause is the DB schema (Booking/User/EventType.destinationCalendar) still being scalar while the domain type is now an array (handleNewBooking.ts:1873-1877 persists only destinationCalendar[0]) — extract a shared helper and/or migrate the schema before the duplication drifts.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly shows the same nested ternary being repeated across many call sites to coerce a scalar DB `destinationCalendar` into the new array-shaped `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` (e.g., bookingReminder.ts, webhook.ts, paypal-webhook.ts, handleCancelBooking.ts, confirm/editLocation/deleteCredential/requestReschedule handlers). The type change is also explicit (`destinationCalendar?: DestinationCalendar[] | null` in CalendarEvent types/class). At the same time, persistence still connects only the first element (`handleNewBooking.ts` uses `connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id }`), evidencing an ongoing scalar DB relationship despite the domain now supporting arrays. This is a concrete maintainability/architecture issue created/exposed by the change (duplication + potential drift), even if it may not be an immediate functional break solely from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The ~20-line block that fetches a credential via prisma.credential.findUnique and manually remaps it field-by-field to CredentialWithAppName is duplicated verbatim in EventManager.ts:343-364 (createAllCalendarEvents) and :503-527 (update), with a third variant in handleCancelBooking.ts:425-434 that omits the app include — extract a single getCredentialById() helper.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows duplicated logic in `packages/core/EventManager.ts` where, if a credential isn’t found in `this.calendarCredentials`, it fetches it from `prisma.credential.findUnique` (with `include: { app: { select: { slug: true }}}`) and then manually remaps fields into a `CredentialWithAppName`-shaped object. This appears in `createAllCalendarEvents` (inside the loop over `event.destinationCalendar`, where `credentialFromDB` is remapped) and again in the calendar-reference update path (loop over `calendarReference`, same fetch+remap). A related but slightly different variant exists in `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts`, where it fetches a credential via `prisma.credential.findUnique` without the app include and without the same remapping. This is a real maintainability/architecture issue introduced by the change (not a functional defect), and extracting a helper like `getCredentialById()` would reduce duplication and inconsistency.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Separation-of-concerns smell in EventManager: it was previously a pure orchestrator over injected calendarCredentials but now queries Prisma directly mid-loop, blurring its boundary.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows EventManager now performing direct Prisma DB lookups inside orchestration loops. In `createAllCalendarEvents`, when a destination has `credentialId` but it isn’t found in `this.calendarCredentials`, it calls `prisma.credential.findUnique(...)` mid-loop to fetch it and then constructs a `CredentialWithAppName` object. Similar DB-fetch fallback logic was added in `updateCalendarEvents` (looping over `calendarReference`) and in `handleCancelBooking` for missing user credentials. This concretely blurs EventManager’s role from coordinating already-provided credentials into also being responsible for persistence access, which matches the separation-of-concerns/architecture smell described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:437-457, the recurring-cancellation branch is completely independent of reference yet sits inside the for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference) loop, so an N-reference booking runs the whole recurring deletion N times (duplicate deleteEvent calls per updated booking, second call 404s) — the branch belongs outside the loop.

adjudication.rationale: In handleCancelBooking.ts the code was changed to iterate `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)` (where `bookingCalendarReference` is now an array via `.filter(...)`). Inside that loop, when `bookingToDelete.eventType?.recurringEvent && bookingToDelete.recurringEventId && allRemainingBookings` is true, it runs a `promises = bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(..._calendar).map(...)` that itself iterates credentials and deletes events for each `updBooking` (via `calendar?.deleteEvent(uid, evt, externalCalendarId)`). That recurring-deletion logic does not depend on the outer `reference` values (it doesn’t use `reference.uid/externalCalendarId` inside the branch), so for N calendar references it will execute the same bulk deletion N times, causing duplicate `deleteEvent` calls for the same updated bookings/calendars (likely leading to 404s on subsequent deletes). This matches the finding that the recurring branch belongs outside the outer loop.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In the recurring-cancellation branch of handleCancelBooking.ts, the outer const calendar = await getCalendar(calendarCredential) is dead (shadowed by the inner const calendar), a wasted call.

The outer `calendar` is not referenced in that recurring branch (it is only used in the non-recurring `else`), so that `await getCalendar(calendarCredential)` is a wasted call in the recurring-cancellation path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: updBooking.references.find(...) in handleCancelBooking.ts still takes only the first calendar reference of each updated booking, so collective members' events on other references are not cleaned up on cancellation.

adjudication.rationale: In packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts, within the recurring-event cleanup path, the code still uses `updBooking.references.find((ref) => ref.type.includes("_calendar"))`, which returns only the first calendar reference for each `updBooking`. Since this diff refactors calendar references/destination calendars to be plural (e.g., `bookingToDelete.references.filter(...)` earlier in the same function), an `updatedBooking` can have multiple `_calendar` references (e.g., collective/team member events). Using `find` means additional calendar references on that booking would not be deleted, so some member calendar events can remain after cancellation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Multi-host destination-calendar selection is implemented only in GoogleCalendarService; Lark (larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:128-130, 163-165, 192-194, 237-239), Office365 (office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:73-76), and BaseCalendarService (packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:156-163) destructure destinationCalendar[0] and use its externalId while EventManager invokes them once per host with that host's credential, so for a collective event with two non-Google hosts, host B's credential is used against host A's calendarId (wrong calendar or API error) — the collective-multi-host feature only works end-to-end on Google.

[]; const calendarId = mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId;`), so when the loop runs for host B it still uses host A’s calendar externalId. adjudication_records.issue_text: In handleNewBooking.ts, teamDestinationCalendars is populated via side effects inside map callbacks, making correctness depend on the later await Promise.all having already run — fragile temporal coupling.

adjudication.rationale: In `handleNewBooking.ts`, `teamDestinationCalendars` is mutated via `teamDestinationCalendars.push(...)` inside the async `map` callback that builds `teamMemberPromises`. The later logic (`await Promise.all(teamMemberPromises);` then `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`) implicitly relies on those side effects having happened. While it likely works today (the push occurs before the first `await` in the callback), it is fragile/temporally coupled and could break if an `await` is introduced before the push or the sequencing changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The new externalId? parameter on CalendarManager.createEvent (packages/core/CalendarManager.ts:219-221, 267-270) is a pure pass-through that never influences event creation and is only echoed into the return object, so it can record a calendar the event was not actually created on (Google falls back to 'primary' when the credentialId find misses).

adjudication.rationale: In packages/core/CalendarManager.ts, the new `externalId?` argument to `createEvent` is never used to influence which calendar the provider writes to; it’s only echoed back in the returned `EventResult` (`externalId, credentialId: credential.id`). Meanwhile, GoogleCalendarService.createEvent selects the calendar purely via `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId` and otherwise falls back to `"primary"` (`calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`). Therefore it is possible for `EventManager` to record `result.externalId` (from the pass-through) that does not match the calendar actually used by the integration (e.g., when the find misses and Google uses `primary`, or when multiple destination calendars share a credentialId and `.find` returns the first one). This is a correctness issue because stored `externalCalendarId` can be wrong.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead-code fallback in Google `CalendarService.ts` updateEvent (253-256) and deleteEvent (314-317): the fallback branch only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy but then searches for a calendar whose `externalId === externalCalendarId` (a guaranteed null/undefined), so the find can never succeed and the API call is made with `calendarId: undefined` — booking references without a stored `externalCalendarId` (which this PR itself manufactures via the no-credentialId path in `createAllCalendarEvents`) can no longer be updated or deleted from Google, leaving stale/orphaned events after reschedule/cancel; the predicate should be `cal.credentialId === credentialId`

adjudication.rationale:
In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, both `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` now compute the calendar id like:

- `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`

When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (the branch that’s supposed to be the fallback), the `.find()` predicate compares `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` where `externalCalendarId` is `null/undefined`, so the find will not select any normal destination calendar entry and will return `undefined`. This makes the fallback effectively dead and risks updating/deleting against an undefined/wrong calendar id (or falling back to `primary` if the call site later defaults), which can leave stale/orphaned events.

This is grounded in the diff: the predicate explicitly uses `externalCalendarId` inside the fallback branch, so it cannot locate a real destination calendar when `externalCalendarId` is missing. The finding’s suggested fix (select by credentialId) is consistent with the new multi-destination design introduced in this PR (e.g., `createEvent` now receives `credentialId` and selects the destination calendar via `cal.credentialId === credentialId`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Only Google resolves the destination calendar per credential: Lark (`larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:127,161,190,237`), Office365 (`office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:71-75`), and CalDAV (`lib/CalendarService.ts:156-162`) services were only mechanically converted to use the first destination's `externalId` regardless of which host's credential is creating the event, so for collective events secondary hosts' event creation fails (swallowed into `success: false`) or lands on the wrong calendar, and references are persisted pointing at calendars where no event exists

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` to an array and `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents()` now iterates each destination and calls `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)` (packages/core/EventManager.ts around the new `for (const destination of event.destinationCalendar)` loop). However, only Google’s service actually selects the calendar based on the credential (`GoogleCalendarService.createEvent(calEventRaw, credentialId)` uses `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find(cal => cal.credentialId === credentialId)` to pick `calendarId`). In contrast, Lark and Office365 mechanically destructure the first element (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []; const calendarId = mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId;`) and CalDAV/BaseCalendarService filters by only the first destination calendar externalId as well. This means when creating events for secondary hosts in collective/team scenarios, those non-Google services will still target the first destination’s `externalId` regardless of which host credential is being used, potentially creating the event on the wrong calendar or failing. Meanwhile `CalendarManager.createEvent` returns `externalId` from the loop input (packages/core/CalendarManager.ts adds `externalId` to the result), so persisted references can point to a calendar where the event was not actually created.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Google `createEvent`/`updateEvent` hardcode the organizer email to the first destination's `externalId` even when writing host B's calendar, misattributing the organizer on every non-first host's copy

adjudication.rationale: In `GoogleCalendarService.createEvent`, the organizer attendee email is set from `mainHostDestinationCalendar` (the first element of `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar`) via `email: mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId ? mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId : calEventRaw.organizer.email`, while the actual `calendarId` used for insertion is selected by matching `credentialId` (`calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId`). When creating events for multiple destination calendars, any non-first destination will still get the organizer email taken from the first destination, matching the finding. The same first-element logic is also used in `updateEvent` for organizer email.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Silent skip in `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` (`packages/core/EventManager.ts:~341-365`): when a destination's `credentialId` is set but the credential is neither in `this.calendarCredentials` nor found in the DB, the `if (credential)` block simply doesn't run — no else, no log, no failure result — so a host whose credential was deleted/disconnected gets no calendar event and no trace while the booking completes 'successfully'

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/EventManager.ts` `createAllCalendarEvents`, inside the `for (const destination of event.destinationCalendar)` loop, when `destination.credentialId` is set the code tries to resolve `credential` from `this.calendarCredentials` and then via `prisma.credential.findUnique(...)`. This matches the finding: the booking can proceed while no calendar event is created for that destination and there’s no trace in this function.

A few lines later, for COLLECTIVE team events, the code does `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`, which is a no-op when `destinationCalendar` is `null` due to optional chaining, silently dropping all collected team member destination calendars. adjudication_records.issue_text: Confirmation and payment-success flows (`confirm.handler.ts:175-179`, `payments/api/webhook.ts:118-120, 228-230`, `paypal-webhook.ts:152-156`) rebuild the `CalendarEvent` from `booking.destinationCalendar` (the single Prisma relation, which `handleNewBooking` only populates with `evt.destinationCalendar[0]`) and never reconstruct the multi-host array, so collective bookings requiring confirmation or payment create calendar events only on the organizer's calendar and the other hosts get nothing

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` to an array and `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` now iterates over `event.destinationCalendar` to create events per destination. However, in `handleNewBooking` the booking persistence only connects the first destination calendar (`connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id }`), so `booking.destinationCalendar` remains a single Prisma relation. The confirmation and payment-success flows shown (`confirm.handler.ts`, `payments/api/webhook.ts`, `paypal-webhook.ts`) rebuild `evt.destinationCalendar` from `booking.destinationCalendar` (or `user.destinationCalendar`) and wrap it into a one-element array, never reconstructing any additional host calendars added for COLLECTIVE (`evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`). Thus, those flows will pass only the organizer (or single) destination calendar into event creation, preventing multi-host/collective destination calendars from being created in those paths.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `EventManager.update` catch block (`packages/core/EventManager.ts:~595-607`): if the throw happens before `calendarReference` is assigned (e.g., the `newBooking` Prisma query fails), the catch returns `calendarReference?.map(...) ?? []` — an empty array instead of the previous guaranteed `success: false` result row — so a thrown update can be recorded as a no-op

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/EventManager.ts`, `calendarReference` was changed from a single `PartialReference | undefined` to `PartialReference[] | undefined` and the catch block now returns `Promise.resolve(calendarReference?.map(...) ?? ([] as Array<EventResult<NewCalendarEventType>>))`. Since `calendarReference` is initialized as `undefined` (`let calendarReference: PartialReference[] | undefined = undefined`) and only assigned after the Prisma queries that can throw, an error occurring before assignment will cause the catch to return `[]` (empty array) instead of the prior behavior which always returned a single `{ success: false, ... }` result. This matches the finding: an update failure can be reported as a no-op.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `EventManager.update` catch block: when a failure happens mid-loop (e.g., `updateEvent` rejecting for one member's unresolvable credential via `Promise.all`), the catch marks every reference `success: false`, turning a partial failure into a total failure — one bad host poisons updates for all other hosts' calendars

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/EventManager.ts` the update path now collects **multiple** `calendarReference`s via `filter(...)` and processes them in a loop. If any exception escapes that loop/try (e.g., a thrown error during credential lookup or a rejected `updateEvent(...)` later aggregated), the `catch` returns `calendarReference.map(...)` with `success: false` for **every** reference (new code: `return Promise.resolve(calendarReference?.map((reference) => { ... success: false ... }))`). This converts a single-reference failure into an all-references failure report, which matches the finding that a partial failure can be reported as total failure across hosts/calendars.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Partial deletion of multi-reference bookings: the merge-delete on `newBookingId` (`EventManager.ts:~555-557`) and the recurring-cancel branch (`handleCancelBooking.ts:~437-450`) still use `.find(...)` first-match-only on the now multi-element reference set, and recurring-cancel iterates only the organizer's credentials (members' credentials are never consulted) — after reschedule/cancel of a collective booking, the other hosts' calendars keep stale events

adjudication.rationale:
The diff explicitly changes calendar references/destination calendars to multi-element arrays, but some cleanup paths still only operate on a single calendar reference.

- In `packages/core/EventManager.ts`, the merge-delete path when `newBookingId` is set still does `const oldCalendarEvent = booking.references.find((reference) => reference.type.includes("_calendar"));` (single match). If a booking now has multiple `_calendar` references (as enabled by the multi-destination changes), only the first will be deleted, leaving stale events.

- In `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts`, the recurring-cancel branch iterates updated bookings and does `updBooking.references.find((ref) => ref.type.includes("_calendar"))` (single match) when deleting, so for bookings with multiple calendar references only one gets deleted per updated booking.

These are correctness defects consistent with the refactor to multi-calendar support and can leave stale events in other hosts’ calendars.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Credentials fetched from DB by raw ID with no ownership validation (`EventManager.ts:~341-357` and `~505-530`, `handleCancelBooking.ts:~425-441`): `prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id } })` uses whatever row comes back without checking that the credential belongs to the booking's user/hosts, expanding the trust boundary from fail-closed to fail-open — a malicious user could point their destination calendar at any credential ID in the database and have bookings write to or cancel/update another user's calendar using their OAuth tokens; needs explicit `userId`/`teamId` scoping on the DB fetch

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new fallback credential lookups by raw primary key with no user/team ownership scoping. In `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`, if a `destination.credentialId` isn’t found in `this.calendarCredentials`, it now calls `prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: destination.credentialId } })` and then uses that credential to `createEvent(...)`. Similarly, in `EventManager.updateCalendarEvent` it does `findUnique({ where: { id: reference.credentialId } })` when the credential isn’t in `this.calendarCredentials`, and in `handleCancelBooking` it does `prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: credentialId } })` if not found under `bookingToDelete.user.credentials`. These are exactly the patterns the finding describes: fetching “whatever row comes back” and then performing calendar operations with it, whereas previously missing credentials would effectively fail-closed (no DB fallback). The diff itself does not show any explicit `userId`/`teamId` check on these DB fetches.
